purpose: Continuously improve how Owner, ChatGPT and Codex build XiaoYou while preserving evidence, stage discipline, safety, project continuity, and non-drifting role ownership.
stable_principles: Owner decides product/business direction and performs final real WeCom acceptance only after ChatGPT confirms the production technical gate is ready.

ChatGPT is the technical lead and GitHub code executor. ChatGPT owns architecture, planning, repo code changes, tests, PR review, evidence/PASS judgment, next-step control and Project Knowledge maintenance.

Codex is a server-side executor/verifier only. Codex inspects server facts, validates candidates, deploys approved GitHub code, restarts/rolls back approved services, and reports evidence. Codex does not independently redesign architecture or take ownership of repo code changes.
When Codex finds a code or architecture blocker, Codex must STOP and report facts. ChatGPT decides the fix and makes the GitHub change; Codex then re-verifies or deploys the new approved candidate.
The Owner is not the default technical relay. The Owner manually passes a Codex brief only when the execution channel is unavailable, and performs real WeCom acceptance when explicitly invited.
One formal capability stage at a time; do not mix unrelated future-stage debt into the current blocker.
Evidence before conclusion: distinguish model self-report, unit tests, isolated integration, production technical facts and real business acceptance.
Freeze acceptance criteria before real testing; fix only blockers and do not move the goalposts during a stage.
Live facts outrank remembered facts; run the appropriate Freshness Gate before code or production work.
Use the smallest general fix that addresses the root cause; do not patch for one prompt or one test case.
Stop after structural failure instead of blind retry loops; establish root-cause evidence before another production attempt.
A major work item is not done until Project Knowledge is synchronized.

current_workflow.name: Orient
current_workflow.action: Read PROJECT_INDEX, Freshness Gate, CURRENT_STATE, ACTIVE_WORK and this Working Method before implementation.

current_workflow.name: Define the single problem
current_workflow.action: State the current-stage proposition, exact blocker, non-goals, evidence needed and stop conditions.

current_workflow.name: Classify responsibility
current_workflow.action: Classify the next action strictly by role: ChatGPT owns architecture/planning/GitHub code; Codex owns server inspection/verification/deployment/rollback; Owner owns product decisions and final real WeCom acceptance. Do not shift repo coding or architecture design to Codex.

current_workflow.name: Inspect before change
current_workflow.action: Trace the relevant code/data/runtime path and distinguish root cause from symptom. For production facts, use read-only server evidence when repository evidence is insufficient.

current_workflow.name: Design the smallest general fix
current_workflow.action: Preserve model-first architecture, authority boundaries, permissions, stage boundaries and rollbackability.

current_workflow.name: Implement in GitHub
current_workflow.action: ChatGPT implements the approved solution in GitHub: branch/PR/tests/review. Codex does not author the product solution or substitute unmanaged server patches for repository code.

current_workflow.name: Verify candidate
current_workflow.action: Run targeted tests plus baseline A/B where relevant. Candidate-only failures determine regressions; an existing baseline failure is not silently reclassified.

current_workflow.name: Server verification/deployment
current_workflow.action: Codex receives a goal-and-boundary-oriented server verification/deployment brief for the GitHub candidate. It may inspect, validate, deploy, restart or roll back within the brief. If it finds a code/architecture blocker, it STOPs and reports facts; ChatGPT fixes GitHub and reissues the gate.

current_workflow.name: Production technical gate
current_workflow.action: Verify actual deployed version, runtime topology, health, authority boundaries and rollback state before real business testing.

current_workflow.name: Owner acceptance
current_workflow.action: Only after ChatGPT judges the production technical gate ready, explicitly tell the Owner to perform the real WeCom/XiaoU acceptance test. The Owner does not replace server verification.

current_workflow.name: Seal or iterate
current_workflow.action: PASS seals the capability with evidence; FAIL fixes only the blocker; BLOCKED resolves the external/structural dependency first.

current_workflow.name: Knowledge sync
current_workflow.action: Update PROJECT_INDEX, CURRENT_STATE, ACTIVE_WORK, Evidence, capability/ADR/history and Working Method when the method itself changed.

stop_rules: Do not repeatedly redeploy after multiple unexplained production failures.
Do not stop/restart production services without a proven safe path and rollback for the current risk.
Do not change business acceptance criteria simply to make a candidate pass.
Do not let a server-only unmanaged patch become the product solution without Git governance.
Do not claim PASS before the required evidence layer is complete.
Do not reopen a sealed capability for non-blocking cosmetic issues.
Do not let current-work urgency bypass Project Knowledge freshness when live facts may have changed.

include: explicit statement that Codex is verifier/deployer, not architecture or repo-code owner
avoid: asking Codex to fix GitHub code when it finds a blocker; it should report the blocker to ChatGPT
prescribing repo implementation when Codex is only the server executor
codex_brief_style.exception: Precise paths/commands may be specified when server execution safety requires an exact controlled action.

method_learning_loop.principle: The working method may evolve, but only through evidence-backed process learning.
triggers: The same class of failure repeats.
A handoff repeatedly loses context or creates contradictory work.
A deployment/check process creates avoidable risk or repeated false blockers.
A new tool/capability enables a materially safer or faster workflow.
The current method creates unnecessary latency, duplication or manual relay.
A new project phase requires a different execution pattern.
process: Observe and record the workflow problem.
Separate a process problem from a product/code problem.
Classify the proposed method change as Class A operational or Class B material.
Propose a candidate method change and expected benefit.
Test the candidate on a bounded work item when practical.
Evaluate evidence: speed, correctness, safety, rework, handoff quality and cognitive load.
For Class B material changes, obtain explicit Owner approval before activation.
Accept, reject or revise the candidate.
If accepted, increment method version, update current method, append a history record and update validator/index.
Never erase the old method; preserve why it was replaced.
forbidden_shortcuts: Do not change the method just because one outcome is inconvenient.
Do not weaken safety/evidence standards merely to move faster.
Do not convert one successful improvisation directly into a permanent rule without enough evidence.
Do not silently change roles or workflow in a new chat window.

success_metrics: Fewer repeated mistakes and reopened decisions.
Faster path from real blocker to verified fix.
Fewer production retries without new evidence.

knowledge_write_protocol.principle: Project Knowledge writes use optimistic concurrency; never overwrite another window's unseen changes.
steps: Read and record project-knowledge HEAD before preparing a material knowledge update.
Immediately before writing, fetch project-knowledge HEAD again.
If HEAD is unchanged, create a commit whose parent is the recorded HEAD and update the ref with force=false.
If HEAD changed, STOP the write, read the intervening knowledge changes, reconcile semantics, re-run consistency checks, then create a new fast-forward commit.
Never force-update project-knowledge to resolve a concurrent edit.
knowledge_write_protocol.conflict_rule: A write conflict is evidence that another window changed project state. Re-read before proceeding; do not treat it as a mechanical Git problem.

class_a_operational.description: Efficiency/refinement changes that do not weaken roles, safety, evidence thresholds, authorization, authority boundaries, stage sealing or production rollback requirements.
class_a_operational.approval: ChatGPT may accept after evidence-backed bounded validation and must version/log the change.

class_b_material.description: Changes to role boundaries, safety guarantees, evidence thresholds, production write/stop authorization, permission/authority semantics, stage order/sealing, or removal of a major guardrail.
class_b_material.approval: Requires explicit Owner approval before becoming the active permanent Working Method.

method_change_governance.emergency_rule: A temporary stricter safety stop may be applied immediately when new risk is discovered; permanent method changes still require normal classification and recording.

must_not: claim Codex executed a task merely because a PR comment or brief exists
delegate architecture ownership or repository coding to Codex by default

owns: candidate verification in the real server environment
approved service restart/start/stop when explicitly authorized
must_not: redesign product or system architecture on its own
take ownership of GitHub product code changes
apply unmanaged server-only patches as the product solution unless ChatGPT explicitly authorizes a bounded emergency action
continue past a structural/code blocker instead of reporting it
codex.blocker_rule: STOP and report server/runtime/code facts to ChatGPT. ChatGPT decides and implements the repository fix, then Codex re-verifies.

owns: explicit approval for Class B working-method changes
final real WeCom/XiaoU acceptance testing after the technical gate
owner.normal_handoff: Owner should not have to design or debug the system. When the Codex execution channel is unavailable, Owner may manually paste the exact ChatGPT-prepared Codex brief and return Codex's factual result.

handoff_sequence: ChatGPT defines the server verification/deployment gate
ChatGPT evaluates evidence and decides the next action
Only after production technical PASS, Owner performs real WeCom/XiaoU acceptance
